crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Rolling Forecasts
children.blurb: Rolling forecasts are budgets and projections that are rebuilt at a fixed cadence, typically monthly or quarterly, so that the planning horizon always extends the same distance ahead.

children.name: External Signals in Revenue Models
children.blurb: External signals in revenue models covers the practice of feeding data from outside a company's own systems into forecasts of sales, bookings and cash.

children.name: Variance Analysis and Explanation
children.blurb: Variance analysis and explanation is the work of comparing what a business actually did against what it planned, then saying why the two differ.

children.name: Capital Spending Decisions
children.blurb: Capital spending decisions in an AI context cover how a company chooses where to commit money for compute, data, talent and tooling, and how those choices are justified to a board or finance committee.

children.name: Zero-Based Budgeting
children.blurb: Zero-based budgeting is a planning method in which every cost line starts at zero and must be justified for the coming period, rather than being carried forward from last year's figure with an adjustment.

sections.body: Forecasting and planning in finance is the work of projecting what a business will earn, spend and need, then revising those projections as facts change. Artificial intelligence now does much of this by fitting models to historical ledgers, pulling in outside data such as order volumes or sector indices, and regenerating a forecast on a schedule rather than once a quarter. In revenue models it links demand signals to expected bookings, and in cost work it flags where actual spending has drifted from plan. The output is a set of numbers a finance team can interrogate, not a verdict, and the models are only as good as the data feeding them.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Rolling forecasts are the most mature use, because the underlying arithmetic is well understood and the main gain is speed and frequency. Variance explanation is partly solved for routine line items and much weaker where a variance comes from a one-off event or a contract change that never appeared in the training data. External signals help most when a company has a clean mapping between the signal and its own revenue, which many do not. Capital spending and zero-based budgeting remain the hardest, because both turn on judgment about strategy and internal politics that no model observes. The honest limit is that a forecast is a distribution, not a number, and most tools still present a single figure with false confidence.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader should start with Rolling Forecasts for the mechanics of continuous projection and how often to refresh. External Signals in Revenue Models then covers what outside data can be brought into the revenue line and where that mapping breaks down. Variance Analysis and Explanation takes the gap between plan and actual and shows how much of the explanation can be automated. Capital Spending Decisions moves from operating numbers to large, infrequent commitments, where the evidence is thinner. Zero-Based Budgeting closes the section by asking what each cost would be if it were justified from scratch, the most judgment-heavy page of the five.
